stories.headline: Nvidia board prepares to oust CEO, name interim chief
stories.claim: Nvidia's board reportedly prepares to oust CEO Jensen Huang after a second extramarital affair, with CFO Colette Kress possibly named interim chief.
stories.summary: Semafor, citing people familiar with the matter, reports that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove founder and CEO Jensen Huang, possibly as soon as Wednesday, after media reports of a second extramarital affair. Some directors reportedly favour naming CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, and an outside search firm has reportedly been hired. Bloomberg reports Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji is among those considered. Nvidia shares reportedly fell over 8% after hours, hitting a 52-week low. The board has also reportedly launched a Wachtell Lipton-led probe into whether Huang divulged corporate secrets, and two US senators asked the administration to preserve related documents.

stories.claim: White House says a woman's laugh heard at the start of Trump's C-SPAN call was leftover audio from a previous caller.

stories.headline: Gas bills to rise as Middle East turmoil persists
stories.claim: Jersey gas customers face a 1p per kWh rise, about 5%, from 1 December 2026 due to Middle East supply disruption.

stories.headline: Helsing launches Clarity, a European rival to Palantir’s Maven
stories.claim: German defence firm Helsing launches Clarity, an AI targeting platform pitched as a European rival to Palantir's Maven.
stories.summary: German defence start-up Helsing has launched Clarity, an AI platform that turns drone, satellite and sensor data into military targets, positioned as a European alternative to Palantir's Maven system. Clarity runs hundreds of military AI agents that share one data model and nominate targets only when independent sources agree, confidence is high and a human operator confirms. Helsing says the software runs on customer-owned infrastructure, follows NATO standards and can connect to weapons from any maker. The launch comes as European governments seek more control over their military software, and France's intelligence service is reportedly replacing Palantir with a homegrown tool. The article also covers Palantir's political and regulatory exposure in the US and UK, including its chief executive's comments and a CISA nomination.

Beijing has rolled out measures in recent years to boost marriage and childbearing, and these have worked in some regions. A prominent Chinese academic has urged the government to plan for immigration, since the shift will have large fiscal costs over decades.

stories.headline: Oil slicks seen from space: the devastating impact of boat strikes on fragile Gulf ecosystems
stories.claim: Greenpeace has logged over 500 oil spills since the US-Iran war began, covering about 20,000 sq km, threatening Gulf ecosystems.
stories.summary: Oil slicks covering an estimated 20,000 square kilometres, roughly the size of Wales, have spread across the Gulf since the US war with Iran began on 28 February. Greenpeace has identified more than 500 spills through satellite monitoring, and October was the worst month with more than 30 attacks on tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz. Scientists warn that oil coating mangroves and birds, combined with shallow warm waters, could cause lasting damage to corals, fish and turtle habitats. Gulf states have launched clean-ups in some cases, but researchers in Iran and the Gulf say they have been told not to speak publicly. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's busiest oil shipping routes, so the attacks also bear on global oil supply and prices.

Cumulative slicks total roughly 20,000 square kilometres, according to Greenpeace's satellite mapping.

Shorelines and protected areas, including Shidvar Island and the Musandam national park, have been affected.

stories.headline: What to know about this year’s UN climate talks
stories.claim: COP31 UN climate talks are under way in Antalya, Turkey, with the US absent and fossil fuels and climate finance in focus.
stories.summary: The UN climate summit COP31 opened on 8 November in Antalya, Turkey, and is due to close on 20 November, with Turkey and Australia as cohosts. The talks come against a tense backdrop: the war in Iran has pushed energy prices up, and the US, which has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement, sends no formal delegation. The UN Environment Programme has warned that warming is likely to pass 1.5C within a few years. Negotiators face the question of how to fund cuts and adaptation, with rich nations giving $136.7 billion in 2024 against a goal of $300 billion a year by 2035. Fossil fuels are another flashpoint, since the 2025 deal did not mention them once.
key_points: COP31 began on 8 November in Antalya and runs until 20 November 2026.
Turkey and Australia are cohosting, and both face criticism over their fossil fuel links.

stories.headline: Strategy, the World’s Biggest Corporate Bitcoin Holder, to Be Dropped From MSCI Indexes
stories.claim: MSCI confirms it will drop Strategy (MSTR) from its MSCI USA, World and ACWI indexes at the close on 30 November 2026.
stories.summary: Strategy, the world's largest corporate bitcoin holder, will be removed from MSCI's flagship equity indexes after the close on Monday, 30 November 2026. The index provider announced the decision late on Wednesday 11 November, under a rule that excludes so-called non-operating companies, meaning firms whose balance sheets are mostly stakes, commodities or crypto rather than operating businesses. Strategy was widely expected to be removed, and its shares fell about 2% in after-hours trading. JPMorgan estimates up to $2.8 billion of Strategy shares could be sold by index funds if MSCI removal happens, with a further $8.8 billion at risk if other major indexes follow. Strategy argues the impact will be limited, as MSCI-tracking funds hold only about 3.1% of its basic shares. The same review adds Moderna and Aritzia to the MSCI World, with 100 deletions across the ACWI.
key_points: MSCI will delete Strategy's common stock (MSTR) from the MSCI USA Index at the close on 30 November 2026, removing it from the MSCI World and ACWI too.
The decision follows a rule introduced in October that excludes non-operating companies, which MSCI treats more like investment funds than operating businesses.
JPMorgan estimates up to $2.8 billion of Strategy shares could be sold through passive rebalancing, rising by a further $8.8 billion if other major indexes follow.
Strategy says MSCI-tracking funds hold roughly 3.1% of its basic shares and that the real impact will be limited; it holds about 850,364 bitcoin.
Michael Saylor criticised MSCI for applying a bias against digital assets, calling the decision a value judgment rather than an objective metric.
Moderna is added to the MSCI USA and Aritzia to the MSCI World; IREN also appears among deletions, though reports do not link it to the new rule.
stories.market_take: Passive selling of up to several billion dollars in early December could pressure Strategy's shares, though the effect is largely expected.

stories.headline: Google gooses Python AI performance by... removing Python
stories.claim: Google has open-sourced XSE, a C++ serving engine that replaces Python in production ML inference.
stories.summary: Google has open-sourced XSE, the XLA Serving Engine, a system that runs machine-learning models without a Python interpreter in the serving path. It already handles more than six million queries per second across services including Search, Google Ads and YouTube Shorts. In Google's tests on short requests, XSE delivered two to five times the throughput of its best optimised Python server while using a quarter of the memory. The tool targets smaller, task-specific models such as ranking and recommendation rather than large language models, which are better served by vLLM or SGLang. It compiles computations via OpenXLA and works best on Google's TPUs, though it also runs on GPUs and CPUs.

stories.headline: Facial recognition errors put ethnic minorities at risk of wrongful arrest, police watchdog warns
stories.claim: UK police inspectors warn that retrospective facial recognition errors and biases risk wrongful arrests of ethnic minorities.
stories.summary: A report from His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary (HMICFRS), published on Wednesday, warns that British police could wrongly arrest innocent people if they treat retrospective facial recognition matches as evidence rather than leads. Inspectors found some investigators did not carry out enough checks before acting on potential matches, and in a few cases officers relied too heavily on the results. The report flags continuing bias in the algorithm, which is more likely to wrongly flag people from ethnic minorities, and says some custody images that should have been deleted were kept. It also notes there is no comprehensive legal framework for the technology. Campaigners such as Big Brother Watch called the findings alarming, while the National Police Chiefs' Council said it remains committed to responsible use.

stories.headline: United Airlines is grounding AI travel agents, and safety is just one of the concerns

stories.summary: United Airlines has begun blocking unauthorised third-party AI assistants from booking flights on behalf of customers, a move that sets it apart from rivals that are opening up to AI agents. The airline says such tools could expose personal data, make unintended purchases, modify bookings or spend MileagePlus rewards without customers noticing. It also argues that certain safety steps, such as passengers confirming their checked bags contain no prohibited items, need direct acknowledgement and could clash with FAA and DOT rules. CEO Scott Kirby told the Wall Street Journal he does not want to create another middleman. stories.claim: eMudhra blames a buggy Python script for issuing weak digital certificates and is quitting the SSL/TLS certificate business.
stories.summary: Indian certificate authority eMudhra says a buggy Python script caused it to issue digital certificates with dangerously weak keys. The error stemmed from a key-generation ceremony on 30 April 2025, when hardware security modules were unavailable because of supply constraints. A Mozilla team member spotted the flaw, browser makers stopped trusting eMudhra's certificates, and the firm has now exited the SSL/TLS business. The company says it will make improvements following an independent review.

stories.summary: The former ocean liner SS United States was scuttled on Wednesday off the Florida panhandle, near Destin and Fort Walton Beach, to create what is expected to be the world's largest artificial reef. stories.headline: New York is forcing T-Mobile to stop putting data caps on low-income home internet plans
stories.claim: New York's attorney general says T-Mobile breached the state's Affordable Broadband Act and T-Mobile agreed to remove data caps on the plans.
stories.summary: New York's Attorney General Letitia James found that T-Mobile was not complying with the state's Affordable Broadband Act, which requires low-cost home internet for eligible low-income households. T-Mobile had applied monthly data caps to its plans, throttling speeds to as low as 650 kilobits per second after 50GB of use, which the state said could happen in about four days of typical use. The company also offered the plans only where it had 5G wireless deployed and blocked search engines from indexing details. Under an agreement, T-Mobile will remove the caps, extend the plans to all places in New York where it offers home internet, and let search engines index the plan details. T-Mobile said it would keep the same low price while updating the plan.
key_points: New York's attorney general found T-Mobile was breaching the Affordable Broadband Act.

stories.claim: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaProof Code, which formally verified Signal's cryptographic core code in four weeks.
stories.summary: Google DeepMind has unveiled AlphaProof Code, an AI system that uses mathematical proofs to show that software meets its security specifications. In a demonstration on Signal's encryption protocol, the team says the work took four weeks, where such work typically takes years. Earlier verification efforts had stopped at the design stage, whereas this one checked the actual cryptographic code running on users' devices. Experts defined the security requirements, and AI agents built on Gemini Carbon wrote more than six million lines in the Lean proof language, with about one percent flagged for human review. Two deliberately planted bugs were caught. Signal's CTO said the approach strengthens trust in privacy, and DeepMind plans to extend the method to power grids and medical devices.

stories.headline: UK fraudster who invented ‘too good to be true’ takeover bid given suspended sentence
stories.claim: UK fraudster who faked a £154m takeover bid for Touchstone Exploration gets two-year suspended sentence.
stories.summary: A British man who invented a fake £154 million takeover bid for Touchstone Exploration has been spared jail. Christopher Woolcott, 44, used ChatGPT to create false bank, law firm and private equity documents, and met the chief executive in person while posing as an American buyer's agent. He had bought shares in the Canadian oil and gas company, which is listed in London, and stood to make about £70,000 if the fake deal had leaked. Southwark Crown Court heard that Touchstone's executives quickly spotted the papers as amateurish. Judge Usha Karu handed him a two-year sentence, suspended for two years, plus 200 hours of community service and £4,627 in costs. The case highlights how easily fabricated deal rumours can be spread on social platforms, and it is a reminder of the market-abuse risks around small-cap takeover speculation.

He had bought Touchstone shares and could have made roughly £70,000 if the fake deal had leaked.
Sentenced at Southwark Crown Court to two years, suspended for two years, with 200 hours of community service and £4,627 costs.
He also promoted the supposed deal on Discord to push up the share price.

Experts say the US, Canada and New Zealand are slowing their climate action.

stories.headline: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?

stories.headline: Quebec’s strategic maple-syrup reserve is running dry
stories.claim: Quebec's strategic maple syrup reserve is nearly empty and expected to be fully depleted by end of February.
stories.summary: Quebec's world-first strategic maple syrup reserve is set to be completely depleted by the end of February, according to the producers' body PPAQ. The reserve, spread across three warehouses and able to hold about 60 million kilograms, was created in 2000 to stabilise prices and supply. Its stock stood at about 18 million kilograms in February, and the PPAQ says strong demand, especially from the United States, has been drawing it down. Quebec produces about 90% of Canada's maple syrup and over 70% of the world's supply. The $1.2 billion industry relies on weather for sap flow, so a bad harvest would leave the market with little buffer. The PPAQ says the reserve needs replenishing and the sector must expand to meet demand. Canadian maple exports are rising, while the reserve's depletion reflects processors buying up stock rather than a shortage at the farm level.
key_points: Quebec's PPAQ says the strategic maple syrup reserve will be completely depleted by the end of February.

stories.headline: Spain: 69 candles lit at Toledo Cathedral for train crash victims
stories.claim: Toledo Cathedral holds a funeral Mass for the 69 victims of Spain's Urda high-speed rail crash.

Residents of Urda placed 69 candles near the altar and a 16th-century sculpture of Christ was brought from the town for the ceremony. The royal couple attended, but Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez did not, citing his refusal to attend religious ceremonies, which drew criticism from opponents. The disaster has already led to the resignations of the transport minister and the head of the railway operator, and European prosecutors have opened a fraud investigation into EU safety funds. A general election is set for 29 November and a train drivers' strike is further disrupting services.

stories.headline: How Martine Rose Became Menswear’s Secret Weapon
stories.claim: Martine Rose has been named Balenciaga's creative director, the first woman to lead the French house.
stories.summary: British-Jamaican designer Martine Rose has been appointed creative director of Balenciaga, the Kering-owned French house. She succeeds Pierpaolo Piccioli, whose departure after three seasons was announced the day before. Rose launched her eponymous label in 2007 and is known for playful, subculture-led menswear and sneaker collaborations with Nike and Supreme. The appointment is a major career step and a historic first for the house, with the challenge being how she scales her idiosyncratic style within a global luxury group.
key_points: Martine Rose is officially Balenciaga's next creative director, succeeding Pierpaolo Piccioli.
She is the first woman to lead Balenciaga as creative director.
Piccioli's departure after three seasons was announced the previous day.
Rose has run her own label since 2007 and previously consulted for Balenciaga from 2015 to 2018.
Kering CEO Luca de Meo issued a statement welcoming the appointment.
stories.market_take: Could be a modest positive for Kering's sentiment if Balenciaga's sales recover under new leadership.

stocks.name: Kering
stocks.reason: Owner of Balenciaga; the new creative director is a key factor in the brand's turnaround.

stories.headline: A Toast To Bianca Saunders: Inside British Vogue And The BFC’s Fashion Fund Dinner
stories.claim: British Vogue and the BFC hosted a dinner in London to celebrate Bianca Saunders, winner of the 2026 Designer Fashion Fund.
stories.summary: British Vogue and the British Fashion Council Foundation held a dinner at Bar Finch in Mayfair to celebrate Bianca Saunders, winner of the 2026 BFC/Vogue Designer Fashion Fund. The prize gives a British-based designer business a £150,000 grant plus mentoring. Saunders won the award in June, and the dinner was hosted by BFC chief executive Laura Weir and Laura Ingham of Vogue's Global Fashion Network. The event is a social celebration rather than a new business development.

stories.headline: From Your Wardrobe to Your Living Room: Reformation Debuts Its First Rug Collection
stories.claim: Reformation launches a nine-rug collection with Les Éditions de Tapis, designed by Thomas Coccimiglio and Lauren Caris Cohan.
stories.summary: Reformation has released its first rug collection, a limited edition of nine hand-knotted rugs created with luxury rug brand Les Éditions de Tapis. The designs were led by Thomas Coccimiglio, founder of Les Éditions de Tapis, and Reformation's chief creative officer Lauren Caris Cohan. The rugs feature motifs such as tigers, swans and palm trees, and are made by artisans in India and Nepal from wool, linen and silk. The partnership grew out of five years of work on the rugs in Reformation's stores, and it extends the brand's aesthetic into the home. The article is a lifestyle and design feature, with no price or financial details given.

stories.headline: “It’s Always About Me and What I Need or What I Want to See Out in the World”: Rick Owens on Reuniting With Adidas
stories.claim: Rick Owens launches a springblade shoe and inflatable-garment collaboration with Adidas, on sale from 17 November.
stories.summary: In an interview, designer Rick Owens discusses his new Adidas collaboration, which uses Adidas's springblade technology. The line includes a gaiter-style boot and runner that were first shown in June at his spring 2027 runway show, along with inflatable garments that will also be produced for sale. Owens says he wants his work to be accessible and wants to avoid wasteful runway sets. The springblade shoes will cost between $590 and $850 and go on sale on 17 November at adidas.com, rickowens.eu and select retailers.

stories.headline: Acer Reports Revenues for October at NT$26.39 Billion, Marking a Five-year High for the Month
stories.claim: Acer reports October revenue of NT$26.39 billion, a five-year high for the month, up 24.3% year on year.
stories.summary: Taiwanese PC maker Acer reported consolidated revenue of NT$26.39 billion for October 2026, up 24.3% from a year earlier and its highest October figure in five years. Year-to-October revenue reached NT$275.94 billion, up 24.0% and the highest for the same period in 13 years. Acer said revenue from businesses other than PCs and displays grew more than 35.9% in the year to October and now makes up 35.3% of group revenue. Publicly listed subsidiaries combined grew revenue 48.2% over the same period. The results point to Acer's diversification strategy gaining traction beyond its core hardware business.
key_points: Acer's October 2026 revenue was NT$26.39 billion, up 24.3% year on year.
Year-to-October revenue of NT$275.94 billion is up 24.0% and is the highest for that period in 13 years.
Businesses other than PCs and displays grew over 35.9% and now provide 35.3% of total revenue.
Revenue from publicly listed subsidiaries rose 48.2% in the year to October.
Acer ITS grew revenue 45.0% and Acer Fashion grew 13.8% in the same period.
stories.market_take: Strong growth in non-PC businesses may support investor interest in Acer's shares in Taipei.

stocks.reason: Record monthly and year-to-date revenue growth from its diversified businesses.

stories.claim: Balenciaga and artist Damien Hirst are releasing a Triple S sneaker, the first drop in a Le City 25th anniversary capsule.
